title: Risk-aware upgrade harness with Terraform preflight and health gating for private runtime
creator: Ava Patel
description: Build a reusable, risk-aware upgrade harness for Private (VPC) data-plane/runtime rollouts that integrates Terraform preflight/IaC checks, staged traffic gating, synthetic health probes, cache priming, and an automated rollback circuit. The harness must be safe-for-production, pluggable into our existing private operator, and provide clear observability and an operator-facing escape hatch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Terraform preflight plan runs and rejects changes that violate resource quotas or networking constraints for at least 90% of customer templates. 2) Rollout engine can execute staged traffic gates with configurable windows (0->5->25->50->100%). 3) Health engine computes a composite health-score (latency, error-rate, evictions, KV hit-rate) and automatically pauses/rolls back when score falls below threshold. 4) Rollback playbook executes non-destructive remediation hooks and can be triggered automatically and manually with audit logs. 5) End-to-end e2e test covering priming, gate fail, and rollback exists in the CI harness.
terraform_modules: Modules to be exercised: vpc/runtime-instance (version >= 3.2.0), runtime/instance-bootstrap, iam/roles-for-runtime. Add a preflight module that runs: resource quota assertions, subnet reachability probe, private-endpoint DNS resolution, and image checksum validation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2287
rollout_plan: Phase A: Canaryless staged gating (no shadow traffic) - traffic windows: 0%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%. Phase B: Optional shadow-mirroring for high-risk customers. Each step waits for a health window (default 3m) and requires health-score >= 0.95 to proceed. If the score drops below 0.9 for two consecutive windows, step is paused and rollback is initiated. Operator can override with an explicit approval that is recorded to the audit log.
health_checks: Primary probes: synthetic-inference (50 qps, 95th latency), kv-cache-hit-rate, gRPC error-rate, host-level CPU/GC outliers. Health aggregator runs every 30s and emits a health-score (0.0-1.0). Thresholds configurable per-customer. Telemetry dashboards: console>deployments>health and Prometheus metrics: rollout_health_score, rollout_step_duration. Alerting: Pager duty if automated rollback triggered.
rollback_playbook: Automated rollback steps: 1) Stop forwarding new traffic to the affected slice. 2) Trigger terraform apply to revert to the last-known-good instance group weights. 3) Run cache-reconcile job to avoid KV mismatch. 4) Run synthetic smoke tests. 5) If smoke tests pass, gradually re-introduce traffic to previous stable bit. Manual steps for operator: open GitHub PR to revert infra changes (link auto-created), escalate to on-call runtime team, and run post-mortem link generation. Runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood/rollbacks/automated-harness
testing_plan: CI: unit tests for health aggregator and preflight module. Integration: ephemeral VPC environment using infra/testbed to run a scripted rollout that exercises gating failure and auto-rollback. Stress test: synthetic traffic at 2x typical peak for 15m during a staged step to validate eviction and latency SLOs. Chaos tests: network partition simulation during priming to ensure safe rollback. Test PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1493
notes: Key tradeoffs: 1) Conservative thresholds reduce blast radius but increase rollout time. 2) Cache priming adds complexity but reduces cold-start errors; we will default to priming for enterprise customers and opt-in for small ones. 3) Terraform preflight will be extended as a library to allow partners to run locally before applying. Timeline: MVP in 4 sprints to unblock initial Dedicated customers.
